scope: GH-006-G product entry: real archives over fixture OpenSSH into a no-Node jail; supervisor-profile resident service; unified bootstrap verbs; capability handshake; admission-closing drains

cases.name: from-zero-install-layout
cases.detail: real archive (27914 files) installed from zero; checks={"current":true,"singleRelease":true,"runtimeId":true,"profiles":true,"bundledNode":true}

cases.name: resident-supervisor-profile-and-handshake
cases.detail: bootstrap start launched the gh-supervisor profile (supervisor pid 2747135); ghRemote/describe answered runtimeId=5d8f8f75, releaseId=vTDQAWQv, admission=open, capabilities=activity-drain+durable-admission+admission-close+runtime-id

cases.name: tunnel-disconnect-survival
cases.detail: the tunnel SIGKILL mid-turn changed nothing: service pid 2747152 stable, a fresh tunnel observed the clean turn end, and the fixture file was written

cases.name: runtime-id-survives-crash-restart
cases.detail: service SIGKILL: the supervisor restarted it (pid 2747152→2747253, restarts=1) and the handshake runtime id stayed 5d8f8f75

cases.name: upgrade-drain-switch-and-data
cases.detail: bootstrap update staged release B, the drain closed admissions (live=false supervisor-report=true), waited the in-flight turn out, and switched (releaseId …JT5qaPuH, new pid 2803914); the home marker survived and the fresh service reopened admissions with the same runtime id

cases.name: rollback-to-previous-release
cases.detail: bootstrap rollback drained and switched back to release A (releaseId …vTDQAWQv) with home data intact

cases.name: gc-pins-and-drops
cases.detail: gc removed the junk release (r-junk) and kept the current, rollback target, and live-pinned releases (vTDQAWQv,JT5qaPuH)

cases.name: concurrent-verbs-serialized
cases.detail: two concurrent use transactions never interleaved: the valid one won (use-ok=0 use-bad=64), the pointer stayed on a real release

cases.name: interrupted-transaction-diagnosis
cases.detail: status named the dead holder's verb (update, interrupted=true); the next verb reclaimed the claim and ran

cases.name: uninstall-preserves-data
cases.detail: uninstall removed the runtimes and supervision state while every other byte of the data root (home, marker, sessions layout) survived

boundaries: the second release is the same tree rebuilt with a variant marker, not a different product version; release identity is the installed release id
machine reboot remains un-simulated (no container privileges); service crash-restart and supervisor-managed switches are real
the resident composition owns no PTY/global leases; its full owned-activity set (running agents + pending inbox) is what the drain waits out — broader resource leases are GH-009
